config.title: Write a frequency counter for words in a sentence

intro.title: Write a frequency counter for words in a sentence
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a frequency counter that analyzes a sentence and counts how many times each word appears. You will learn to use JavaScript objects to store and track these word counts as key-value pairs. The main constructs involved are string manipulation methods like `split()` and loops for iteration. By the end, you'll have a working function that takes any sentence as input and returns an object with each word and its frequency.
intro.usecase: Word frequency counters are essential in text analysis features across many applications. Search engines use them to identify popular keywords and improve search relevance in their results pages. Content platforms like Medium or blogging tools implement them in their dashboards to show writers their most-used terms and writing patterns. Social media analytics tools display word clouds and trending topics using this same counting logic to visualize popular discussion themes.

objectives: Initialize a function to accept a sentence as input.
Apply string methods to split the sentence into individual words.
Construct an object to store word frequencies.
Implement a loop to iterate through the array of words.
Manipulate the frequency object to increment counts for each word.
Control the function to return the final frequency object.
Integrate the frequency counter into a simple script that logs results.

steps.instruction: Inside your frequencyCounter function, create a for loop that iterates through each word in the words array you created in the previous step.
steps.hint: Use a standard for loop with a counter variable (like i) that goes from 0 to words.length. You can access each word using words[i] inside the loop body.
